subject: Mathematics
title: Definite Integrals
summary: A definite integral ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx is a number — the signed area under the graph (positive above the x-axis, negative below). Fundamental theorem: find an antiderivative F, then F(b) − F(a).
Most JEE questions are solved with PROPERTIES rather than direct integration: King's property (x → a + b − x), odd/even, periodicity, and splitting at break points (|x|, [x]).
When the upper limit is a function of x, differentiate with the Leibniz rule. Turn 'limit of a sum' questions into ∫₀¹ f(x) dx.
Memorise a few standard results: Wallis' formula (sinⁿ, cosⁿ), ∫₀^{π/2} log sin x dx = −(π/2) log 2, and ∫₀^{π/2} sinⁿx/(sinⁿx + cosⁿx) dx = π/4.

formulas.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
formulas.formula: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a),   where F′(x) = f(x)
formulas.note: The constant C cancels — no need to write it.

formulas.name: Leibniz rule
formulas.formula: d/dx ∫_{g(x)}^{h(x)} f(t) dt = f(h(x)) h′(x) − f(g(x)) g′(x)
formulas.when: Derivative when the limits contain x.
formulas.mistake: Apply the chain rule only to the limits, not to the variable inside.

formulas.name: Dummy variable and reversing limits
formulas.formula: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(t) dt;   ∫ₐᵇ f = −∫_b^a f;   ∫ₐᵃ f = 0

formulas.name: Splitting the interval
formulas.note: Split only at break points (where the sign/value inside changes).

formulas.name: King's property
formulas.formula: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a + b − x) dx;   ∫₀ᵃ f(x) dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(a − x) dx
formulas.when: When x → (a + b − x) makes a 'pair' — I + I = 2I.
formulas.note: ADD the original and the new integral, then divide by 2.

formulas.name: Even and odd functions
formulas.mistake: First check whether f(−x) = f(x) or −f(x).

formulas.name: Property for 0 to 2a
formulas.formula: ∫₀^{2a} f = 2∫₀ᵃ f  if f(2a − x) = f(x);   = 0  if f(2a − x) = −f(x)
formulas.when: Trig integrals from 0 to π or 0 to 2π.

formulas.name: Periodic functions
formulas.formula: f with period T: ∫₀^{nT} f = n ∫₀ᵀ f;   ∫ₐ^{a+T} f = ∫₀ᵀ f

formulas.name: Wallis formula
formulas.formula: ∫₀^{π/2} sinⁿx dx = ∫₀^{π/2} cosⁿx dx = [(n−1)(n−3)…]/[n(n−2)…] × (π/2 if n even, 1 if n odd)
formulas.when: sinⁿ or cosⁿ from 0 to π/2.

formulas.name: Standard results
formulas.formula: ∫₀^{π/2} log sin x dx = ∫₀^{π/2} log cos x dx = −(π/2) log 2;   ∫₀^{π/2} sinⁿx/(sinⁿx + cosⁿx) dx = π/4

formulas.name: Limit as a sum
formulas.formula: lim_{n→∞} (1/n) Σ_{r=1}^{n} f(r/n) = ∫₀¹ f(x) dx;   general: ∫ₐᵇ f = lim h Σ f(a + rh),  h = (b − a)/n
formulas.note: r/n → x, 1/n → dx. If r runs from 0 to n or 1 to 2n, the limits change (up to 2n → 0 to 2).

formulas.name: Substitution in definite integrals
formulas.formula: x = g(t) ⇒ dx = g′(t) dt and change the limits too: a → g⁻¹(a), b → g⁻¹(b)
formulas.note: Once the limits are changed there's no need to return to x.

formulas.name: Integration by parts (definite)
formulas.formula: ∫ₐᵇ u v′ dx = [u v]ₐᵇ − ∫ₐᵇ u′ v dx
formulas.when: Products (x eˣ, x sin x, log x).

formulas.name: Bounds (estimation)
formulas.formula: m ≤ f ≤ M on [a, b] ⇒ m(b − a) ≤ ∫ₐᵇ f ≤ M(b − a);   |∫ f| ≤ ∫ |f|
formulas.when: 'In what range does the integral lie' questions.

examples.title: King's property (pair)
examples.problem: ∫₀^{π/2} sin x / (sin x + cos x) dx = ?
examples.solution: I = ∫ sin x/(sin x + cos x). With x → π/2 − x: I = ∫ cos x/(cos x + sin x). Adding: 2I = ∫₀^{π/2} 1 dx = π/2 ⇒ I = π/4.

examples.title: Odd function
examples.solution: f(−x) = (−x)³ cos(−x) = −x³ cos x ⇒ odd ⇒ integral = 0, without integrating.

examples.title: King + odd-even mix
examples.solution: x → π − x: I = ∫ (π − x) sin x/(1 + cos²x). Adding: 2I = π ∫₀^π sin x/(1 + cos²x) dx. With t = cos x: = π ∫₋₁¹ dt/(1 + t²) = π × π/2 ⇒ I = π²/4.

examples.title: Limit as sum
examples.problem: lim_{n→∞} (1² + 2² + … + n²)/n³ and lim_{n→∞} Σ_{r=1}^{n} n/(n² + r²) = ?
examples.solution: First: (1/n) Σ (r/n)² → ∫₀¹ x² dx = 1/3.  Second: (1/n) Σ 1/(1 + (r/n)²) → ∫₀¹ dx/(1 + x²) = π/4.

examples.title: Log-sine standard result
examples.solution: I = ∫ log sin x = ∫ log cos x (King). 2I = ∫₀^{π/2} log(sin 2x / 2) dx = ∫ log sin 2x − (π/2) log 2. With 2x = t the first part becomes I ⇒ 2I = I − (π/2) log 2 ⇒ I = −(π/2) log 2.

examples.title: By parts
examples.solution: u = x, v′ = eˣ: [x eˣ]₀¹ − ∫₀¹ eˣ dx = e − (e − 1) = 1.

topics.title: Meaning of a definite integral
topics.explain: Area under a curve: the sum of thin rectangles (width h, height f) as h → 0. So 'limit of a sum' and the integral are the same thing. The part below the x-axis counts negative — for actual area integrate |f|.

topics.title: When to use which property — quick checklist
topics.explain: 1) Limits from −a to a? → check odd/even. 2) Limits 0 to a or a to b with a sin/cos or x/(a+b−x) type pair? → King. 3) |…|, [x], {x}, max/min inside? → split at break points. 4) Periodic function over a long interval? → split into periods. 5) Limit of a sum? → (1/n)Σ f(r/n).

topics.title: Real use of King's property
topics.explain: When f(x) + f(a + b − x) simplifies (like sin + cos, or x + (π − x) = π). Also to remove a factor of x: ∫₀^π x f(sin x) dx = (π/2)∫₀^π f(sin x) dx.

topics.title: Uses of the Leibniz rule
topics.explain: Derivatives of functions defined by integrals with x in the limits, maxima–minima, and 0/0 forms like lim x→0 (∫₀ˣ …)/xⁿ — L'Hôpital and Leibniz together.

topics.title: Recognising a limit of a sum
topics.explain: Write the summation as (1/n) × f(r/n) by taking n outside. r from 1 to n ⇒ 0 to 1; 1 to 2n ⇒ 0 to 2; n+1 to 2n ⇒ 1 to 2.

topics.title: Limits under substitution
topics.explain: When substituting in a definite integral, change the limits to the new variable. If the substitution isn't one-one (e.g. t = sin x on 0 to π), you may need to split the interval.

topics.title: Connection to area
topics.explain: Area between two curves = ∫ (upper − lower) dx between the intersection points. This is the base of the next chapter (Application of Integrals).

ratta: ∫₀^π x f(sin x) dx = (π/2) ∫₀^π f(sin x) dx.
